According to the latest issue of the Power On newsletter, Apple was reportedly once considering adding a feature to its "Apple Upgrade" program that would make the process of switching to a new iPhone almost seamless: user data would be transferred before the new device ships. However, this feature never actually came to fruition.

The concept is simple: if users are upgrading their devices on a regular fixed monthly instalment plan, why not make the transition as convenient as possible? Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reported:

There are some obvious loopholes here. First, your iCloud backup will be slightly out of date, because data can only be transferred at the moment of shipment, which is a few days after ordering, unless you choose to pick up the device in person at a store.

Beyond that, there are also obvious privacy concerns. That said, if you've always been using iCloud backup, it's no surprise that Apple has your data. But average users might worry about how the data is transferred to the new phone, and whether anyone has accessed it during the process.

Two years ago, Apple fully rolled out a brand-new system called "Presto" across its retail stores, allowing staff to update the software while the iPhone is still in the box. It's not hard to imagine extending this system in the future to support iCloud backup transfers, without anyone touching your data throughout the process.

However, this feature ultimately never made it to market — and that might actually be a good thing.
